Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we stay aligned: 

1) Recap of discovery
- Primary use case: real-time customer support scoring + multi-turn generation for EU + US customers.
- Key requirements: 99th percentile latency under 300ms for short prompts, EU data residency, predictable throughput during peak hours, and clear unit economics compared to hyperscaler endpoints.

2) How Redwood differentiates (short)
- Multi-region routing with consistent API: same endpoint but requests served from nearest region with automatic fallback to compatible model variants.
- Cost controls: intelligent batching + prefix caching and quantization profiles tuned per workload to reduce token costs without regression.
- Observable SLOs: token-level latency/cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards for investigating regressions.

3) Immediate next steps (what we offered)
- We propose a 48–72 hour multi-region performance run vs your current hyperscaler setup (you can share a short sample workload). We'll spin up test endpoints in us-west2 and eu-west1 and collect p50/p95/p99 and tail latencies as well as token cost estimates.
- We'll include a direct comparison matrix (attached) vs the hyperscaler defaults you mentioned.
- Please share IP allowlist (or a short window for open tests), sample payloads (typical prompt size, token mix), and any compliance constraints (PII handling).

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix.pdf, latency-sample-logs.json

If that plan looks good I can coordinate scheduling with Jordan (routing + test harness) and Vivek (solutions/workload tuning).

Best,
